title: DaisyRose-27B: Pushing the Frontier of Post-Training Efficiency
gist: RadixArk released DaisyRose-27B (Apache 2.0), an RL post-train of Qwen3.8-27B on ~1,200 curated long-horizon agent tasks in 18 days on 144 H200s, doubling Terminal-Bench 4.1 pass@1 (5.6% to 12.0%) and improving every reported benchmark. The release doubles as a showcase for RadixArk's efficiency stack: fully asynchronous RL via Miles with 37% MFU (vs 16% for the Megatron-based open-source trainer, 57% less GPU time), 2x end-to-end throughput, and an AgentENV-based sandbox service ~80% cheaper than popular cloud sandbox providers.

insights.claim: RadixArk released DaisyRose-27B, its first model, an Apache 2.0 reinforcement-learning post-train of Qwen3.8-27B using the Miles framework, shipped in BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 checkpoints.
insights.speaker: Jason Chen
insights.so_what: Another open-weight derivative built on Qwen shows Chinese base models anchoring the Western open post-training ecosystem.

insights.claim: DaisyRose-27B was trained on just ~1,200 curated long-horizon agent tasks with sessions up to 1M tokens in 18 days on 144 H200 GPUs, and improved Terminal-Bench 4.1 pass@1 from 5.6% to 12.0%.
insights.speaker: Jason Chen
insights.so_what: Large agentic gains from small, targeted RL datasets imply post-training, not pretraining scale, is where cheap capability gains are for mid-size open models.
insights.quote: with just 1,200 curated tasks in 18 days on 144 H200 GPUs

insights.claim: DaisyRose-27B beat base Qwen3.8-27B on every reported benchmark: Terminal Bench 2.1 (73.0 to 75.5), DeepSWE v1.1 (42.2 to 46.2), SWE Bench Pro v2 (91.3 to 94.7), HLE text-only (33.9 to 34.3), IFBench (79.5 to 82.4) and GPQA Diamond (89.2 to 90.7), with scores taken as the higher of BF16 and FP8 runs.
insights.speaker: Jason Chen
insights.so_what: Gains outside agentic tasks are small (HLE +0.4); the RL recipe mainly lifts long-horizon agent/coding performance, with best-of-two-precision reporting a mild caveat.

insights.claim: RadixArk recommends serving DaisyRose-27B with SGLang and DSpark speculative decoding; the model retains Qwen3.8-27B's architecture, tokenizer, image understanding and 256K-token context, and reasons by default before answering.
insights.speaker: Jason Chen
insights.so_what: Reinforces SGLang as a default open inference stack tied to the RadixArk ecosystem.

insights.claim: RadixArk built DaisyRose training tasks with Eigent AI, filtering thousands of candidates to about 1,200 by redesigning each task around a mistake the base model makes and tuning difficulty until the solve rate fell within a useful learning range.
insights.speaker: Jason Chen
insights.so_what: Error-targeted, difficulty-calibrated curricula are a replicable recipe; curated agent-task data is becoming a valuable input market.
insights.quote: We ran Qwen3.8-27B on every task and redesigned each one around the mistakes we wanted the model to stop making.
insights.locator: We selected tasks using three criteria

insights.claim: Each DaisyRose training attempt ran up to 1.5 hours in a sandbox with more than 100 tool calls and more than 256K output tokens, requiring multi-step interdependent reasoning, planning and execution.
insights.speaker: Jason Chen
insights.so_what: Long-horizon RL rollouts this heavy make sandbox and inference capacity, not trainer compute, the dominant cost driver of agent post-training.
insights.quote: Each attempt gets up to 1.5 hours in a sandbox, with more than 100 tool calls and more than 256K output tokens.
insights.locator: Each task requires several interdependent steps

insights.claim: RadixArk reviewed every task alongside model attempts and fixed or removed tasks that could be passed without solving the intended problem, guarding against reward hacking.
insights.speaker: Jason Chen
insights.so_what: Reward-hacking-resistant task verification is a key quality differentiator for RL environment vendors.
insights.quote: Tasks must reward actually solving the problem.
insights.locator: Tasks must reward actually solving the problem

insights.claim: RadixArk trained DaisyRose-27B with Miles in fully asynchronous mode: 128 H200s ran agent inference while 16 H200s ran the trainer, with updated weights pushed to the inference fleet after every step so neither side waits.
insights.speaker: Jason Chen
insights.so_what: An ~8:1 inference-to-training GPU split in agentic RL shows post-training compute is overwhelmingly inference, favoring inference-optimized hardware and serving stacks.
insights.quote: the agent keeps working while the model learns, and neither waits for the other

insights.claim: RadixArk's internal training backend reached 37% model FLOPs utilization versus 16% for the Megatron-based open-source trainer on comparable runs, meaning 57% less GPU time for the same training.
insights.speaker: Jason Chen
insights.so_what: Software-side MFU gains of this size directly cut RL post-training cost, a competitive lever for training-infrastructure startups.
insights.quote: So the same training needs 57% less GPU time.

insights.claim: RadixArk claims its backend's efficiency advantage over the open-source trainer is larger on mixture-of-experts models: 6.2x on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and more than 10x on the roughly 300B-parameter GLM-5.3-Flash.
insights.speaker: Jason Chen
insights.so_what: As MoE dominates open models, open-source RL trainers appear notably inefficient on them; a gap infra vendors can monetize.
insights.quote: The gain is even larger on mixture-of-experts models

insights.claim: The DaisyRose-27B release run achieved about 16,800 training tokens per second end to end across 144 GPUs versus about 8,300 for the open-source trainer on the same GPUs, and held steady over 63,000 total GPU-hours.
insights.speaker: Jason Chen
insights.so_what: 2x end-to-end throughput with multi-week stability suggests production-grade RL infra, reducing the GPU budget needed for competitive agent post-training.

insights.claim: RadixArk's sandbox service, built on the open-source AgentENV project, ran about 944,000 sandboxes between mid-September and mid-November with up to 1,566 concurrent, scaling from one to 12 machines while shipping ten upgrades mostly mid-training.
insights.speaker: Jason Chen
insights.so_what: Sandbox orchestration at ~1M-run scale is now core infrastructure for agent RL, a growing market for sandbox providers.
insights.locator: Our service is built on the open-source AgentENV project

insights.claim: RadixArk's sandbox creation success rate was 99% across nine weeks and exceeded 99.95% since late October.
insights.speaker: Jason Chen
insights.so_what: Reliability of environments is a gating factor for long RL runs; failures waste expensive rollout compute.
insights.locator: The service grew from one machine

insights.claim: RadixArk says its sandbox cloud infrastructure cost about 80% less than running the same sandboxes on popular cloud sandbox providers, partly by letting each sandbox's memory allocation grow and shrink with actual usage to pack more sandboxes per machine.
insights.speaker: Jason Chen
insights.so_what: Implies pricing pressure on hosted agent-sandbox vendors as large RL users self-host with elastic memory packing.
insights.quote: about 80% lower than running the same sandboxes with popular cloud sandbox providers
insights.locator: Cloud infrastructure costs for the project
